title: Apple Special Event, September 2008
speaker: Steve Jobs
content:
Good morning.

Thank you. Thank you for coming this morning. We got some really exciting stuff to share with you. Uh, before we do, I just wanted to mention this.

Enough said. So, let's get on with the real topic of this morning, which is music. We're going to talk about music today and got some really fun new offerings. So, let's start with iTunes. iTunes, of course, is the ubiquitous music and video player, married with the largest online content store in the world. And iTunes now offers over 8 and a half million songs. It's amazing. We started off with 200,000. We now have over 8 and a half million songs. Over 125,000 podcasts. Over 30,000 episodes of TV shows, 2,600 Hollywood movies, and as a very recently, we now offer over 3,000 applications for iPhone and iPod Touch. 3,000 apps.

And over the years, we've built up a great customer base. We're very pleased to announce that we've got over 65 million accounts in iTunes now. It's fantastic. 65 million customers, credit cards, one-click shopping. So, this has enabled us to slowly climb up in the US to become the number one music distributor in any format in the US.

So, we're adding some new content to iTunes today. The first thing we're adding is HDTV shows.

Now, you can buy TV shows for $1.99 in standard def on iTunes today. The high-def shows will be just a dollar more at $2.99, and you can watch them on your computer. This is a first. So, you can watch them on Apple TV and you can watch them on your computer. The second thing we're adding is that NBC is coming back to iTunes for this season.

And they're bringing, they're bringing all their great shows with them. So, The Office is coming back, uh, Battles, uh, Monk, uh, Battlestar Galactica, 30 Rock, Heroes, all these great shows and more. And these shows are coming back not just in standard def, but they're coming back in high def as well. So again, you can watch all these shows in standard def or you can watch them in high def right on your computer. Maybe the biggest thing though, with iTunes today, is we're introducing iTunes 8, the next major release of iTunes. It's got a ton of new stuff in it, uh, but I want to cover the few main pieces. Uh, the biggest one, uh, biggest ones are of course HDTV shows, which we just discussed, accessibility. Uh, we've had a lot of requests for this. We've built in voiceover and all of our other accessibility technologies into iTunes, so it's accessible now to even more people. We've got some new browsing in iTunes, which we think you'll like, and we've got something called Genius. So, let's take a look at the last two. Browsing. The way to browse albums up till today has been this. This is the best we've offered. You could look at things by albums, but it's not so space efficient, especially if you only have a few tracks per album. So, what we're adding in iTunes 8 is the ability to just look at your albums by album cover. And we've added this little bar at the top, right? Albums, artists, genres, and composers, and you can look at anything graphically by album art in these four categories. So, you can go from from albums to artists and see little tiles of all of your artists and you can skim these just like an iPhoto and see all the albums that you have of that particular artist. This also scales to of course movies, TV shows, showing you the episodes you might not have watched in a particular series, podcasts, the same thing, but of course it'll get used most for music. So, that's some new browsing, which is really, really nice. And we're introducing a new feature called Genius. Genius is pretty cool. What Genius does, it allows you to automatically make playlists from songs in your music library that go great together with just one click. So, if you could take your library and pull together playlists of songs that just really work together, it helps you rediscover music in your own music library and make great playlists that you probably wouldn't think of making any other way, and it really works well with just one click. So, that's what Genius is. And here's what it looks like. Let's say you're listening to a song, in my case, a Bob Dylan song, Don't Think Twice It's Alright. There's a button down here in the corner, the Genius button. You push that and voila, you've made a Genius playlist. You can refresh it as much as you want, make different playlists, 25 songs, 50 songs, 75 songs, or 100 songs each. And they're amazingly, amazingly good. In addition to that, you can bring up the Genius sidebar, which makes recommendations from the iTunes store of stuff you might want to buy to complete this collection and songs like this. Albums, songs, and songs by other artists that are going to go great with these songs. So, how does this all work? Well, we've got the iTunes store up in the cloud and we've added Genius algorithms to that. We've developed them. We think they're pretty good. And so you've got your music library and if you turn on Genius, it's an opt-in voluntary thing, you turn it on, it's going to send up some information to iTunes. It's going to send information about your music library. Things like track names, play counts, ratings, and playlists so that we can learn about your musical tastes. And this information is sent completely anonymously. At no time do we keep your IDs around. Completely anonymously. But it's not just information from you, right? Because we are going to combine your information with the knowledge of millions of other iTunes users as well. And so you're going to send your information up and so are they. And as that happens, Genius just gets smarter and smarter and smarter. And so everybody benefits by that. And when we send back down results, we send back down Genius results to you and they are tailored to your music library. And as long as you leave Genius turned on, they are automatically updated once a week to take advantage of ever new knowledge that it's gaining as other people share information about their libraries with the Genius, uh, algorithms as well. So, automatically make playlists from songs in your library that go great together with just one click. That's what Genius is about and I'd love to show you this stuff now.

So, let me launch iTunes 8 here. And uh, you can see I've got albums up here. I can click to artists and I can scroll through artists' albums I might have. If I have multiple albums per artist. So, I can, let me go to Aretha Franklin here and open this up. And just, you know, play songs. It's that simple. And this works great as well for uh, you know, genres here. I can see my music by genre. All the albums I have, jazz albums, blues albums, pop albums. And uh, I can even see them by composer if I want to, which is really nice. It also works great for my movies, my TV shows, right? Let me show you an HDTV show by the way. They're really nice. Uh, yeah, here's a nice one from The Office I was playing earlier. Oops.

You get the idea. So, here we are watching HDTV shows right on our iMac here. It's very nice. So, I'm going to go back to music here and uh, I'm going to go uh, search for uh, John Mayer. And uh, I'm going to pick Continuum and I'm going to pick uh, Gravity here, let's say. And all I do is I go down and I push this Genius button right here. And boom, I've made a Genius playlist. Again, it could have been, it's 25 songs, could have been up to 100 songs if I want. I could refresh it, get different songs. But here are songs that go with that song.

All right, let me go back and uh, I'm going to go back to music and I'm going to go find another one here. Just to show you. All right, all albums, Elvis. And uh, I'm going to pick Heartbreak Hotel here.

Let me make a Genius playlist out of that.

And again, it's pulled together songs that go together with that song.

And I'm going to go back to Heartbreak Hotel here and I'm just going to bring out the Genius sidebar and again, it shows me some Elvis albums that I don't own, some top Elvis songs that I'm missing, and uh, some songs by other artists that I might really want to add to my collection if I love these songs.

So, we think you're really going to like the Genius playlist feature. It's really nice.

So, that's iTunes 8 and it's available today as a free download at apple.com. So, go get it and try it out and let us know what you think. So, that's iTunes. Now, let's go talk about the iPod some. The latest data we have is for July. NPD data shows iPod with a 73.4% market share in the US. Uh, we're obviously thrilled with that. Number two is actually other. It's these hundreds of no-name brands that aggregated all together is is number two in the market. Number three is SanDisk with about a little over 8% and number four is Microsoft with 2.6%. So, this is what the market looks like today. And uh, as you know, there are over 5,000 accessories for iPod. It's an incredibly thriving ecosystem. Uh, they announce products even before we want them to. So, it's uh, funny. And uh, and 90% of all new uh, cars in the US now offer iPod integration. So, we're really thrilled with that.

And the cumulative iPod sales since we started are now over 160 million.

So, with that, I'd like to now tell you about some updates and some new products we've got for this holiday season. Let's start off with the iPod Classic. Now, the iPod Classic is the iPod that started it all and uh, we've offered it in two models, a thin and a thick, but almost everybody has wanted the thin one. And so we're going to discontinue the thick and just focus on the thin one. Uh, it's held 80 gigabytes for $249. As of today, we're upgrading the 80 gigabytes to 120 gigabytes at the same $249. So, iPod Classic for this holiday season. We started off, we started off with a thousand songs in your pocket and you can now put 30,000 songs in your pocket. So, it's pretty amazing. So, that's the iPod Classic for this holiday season. Now, let's move on to the Nano. You know, we shipped the first Nano three years ago in 2005. It's only been three years. This was our first generation. Then we had our second generation Nano. This was really a beloved product, the metal and the incredible colors. And then we had our third generation product in 2007, putting a much higher resolution display on for video and and other things where you really want some, some uh, just a beautiful, gorgeous display. But we have a new iPod Nano for this holiday season. Let me show it to you now. This is it right here. It's really, really beautiful. And it combines, it combines the best of both worlds, the portrait aspect ratio that people loved and the same, exactly the same super high res display in portrait mode. And yet, it is the thinnest iPod we've ever made. It is really beautiful. You can see it's an oval shape and it fits in beautifully, as you can see, with the line. The first and second generation portrait, but exactly the same high res screen. I happen to have one in my pocket. Let's go ahead and turn the camera on. This is what it looks like here. And uh, let's zoom in on it. Let me just turn it sideways here and really see it like this. See it like that, what it really looks like. That cool? Very beautiful. So, I think when you actually see one of these things, you're going to just be blown away with how beautiful it is and how thin it is. Okay. So, what are some of the features of this new iPod Nano? Well, a new curved aluminum design. It's got curved glass over the display. The glass actually curves. It's very nice, very durable. It's the thinnest iPod we've ever built. It's got an enhanced user interface with some really nice features. We've taken the accelerometer from the iPhone and the iPod Touch and we've brought it to the iPod Nano and it does some wonderful things. And you can actually create Genius playlists right on the Nano itself, even when it's not connected to iTunes. So, let's take a look at some of these user interface enhancements. With this high res display, you can have beautiful, nice long menus. This is what it's like to look at songs now. We're displaying the albums they come from. And with the accelerometer, you just turn your iPod Nano sideways, you're in cover flow. It's really nice. And then pick a song and go back there. You get full size album art. Now playing screens. Again, with photos, just turn the Nano to see a photo in landscape mode. Video is fantastic on this high res display. And uh, another cool thing is you push

and hold down the center button, you get a pop-up menu, and you can start a genius playlist right on the iPod Nano.
You can add songs to album on the go.
You can browse the album, you can browse the artist, all just by holding that center button down.

It's very, very nice.
We have extras that we normally ship, calendar, stopwatch.
There's even a voice recording program on, so when it detects a microphone, you can record voice notes to yourself.
It's very, very nice and if you'd like, I'd love to show it to you.

So, let me just, you know, play around with it a little bit.
Um, let's go into music, and let's go into artists here.
And we'll pick, uh, uh, let's see.
Oops.
Pick Beck.
And, uh, oh, let's see.

And so, while my music's playing, I can just rotate this sideways, and I'm in cover flow.
Back.

And I think I'll pick, uh, Don't Think Twice, It's All Right.
Uh, come on.
And now, there I am, listening to that.
And I can push down the center button, and I can even start a genius playlist based on those songs right there.
It's created for me right on my iPod.
There's a Donovan song.
Go to the next one.
And so it's taken the songs that I have on my iPod, and it's made a genius playlist right on the go.
Not connected to iTunes or anything else.
Now, one other really cool thing about the accelerometer, is we have a new feature called Shake to Shuffle.
You just take your iPod, shake it, and I just turned on shuffle.

I didn't really want to tell you I had Dean Martin on my iPod, but if you don't like that song, just shake it and you'll get another one.
Isn't that cool?
So, shake to shuffle.

Okay.
So, let's go back and, uh, we'll go to, uh, just photos.
I just want to show you that too.
And, let's see.
Yeah, Zach Lake.
Here's some photos and again, we can just thumb through the photos.
They're beautiful high-res display and of course, it won't take too long before we get to one in landscape and again, we just tilt the unit, go to landscape, take a look at some photos there and, you know, back to portrait here.
And it just works really, really well.
So, that's what I wanted to show you on the iPod Nano.

So, we've got some great, great new features.
And, uh, we've also got some great battery life, 24 hours for music and four hours for video from the thinnest iPod we've ever made.
I think that's a real accomplishment.

Now, another accomplishment is we want to be, uh, just really environmentally sensitive with these products.
We ship a lot of them.
We're constantly worried about reducing the size of the packaging and the transportation carbon that we spend to move these around the world.
But the the biggest thing we worry about are the toxics.
And we have an environmental checklist we use internally, uh, on everything.
And, uh, I have to say the new iPods are looking great from this point of view.
They're arsenic-free glass, they're BFR-free, they're completely mercury-free, and they're PVC-free.
And they're highly recyclable materials, the aluminum and the glass, highly recyclable.
So, uh, we're really trying our best.
There's more we're going to do in the future, but so far, uh, we think these new Nanos are the cleanest, toxic-free, uh, iPods we've ever built.

Now, there's one thing I haven't really talked about with the new Nanos, which we call Nanochromatic.
They come in some amazing colors, the best colors we've ever done.
Johnny and his team came up with some just some fantastic colors and here's, here's what they are.

Now, normally, normally they come up with some colors like this and we pick a few of them.
We decided to do all of them.
And, uh, so we're doing all these colors in all the models.
We have two models.
The first one is going to have an entry price of $149 with 8 gigabytes of memory.
That's our highest memory we've ever had.

And we're going to have a second model with 16 gig at 199.

And both of these are shipping out of our factories.
Uh, the 8 gig should be in stock in the next few days.
The 16 gigs, uh, hopefully this weekend, uh, early next week at the latest.
So, we're really, really happy about this.
And, uh, we've also got some great accessories that we're announcing today.
Of course, uh, we have the requisite armband, which is, which is nice.
Uh, but we've got some headphones as well.
We've got a pair of headphones we're going to be introducing.
Now you can say, well, why do you need headphones?
You've headphones that come with the Nano.
Well, these headphones have something on the cable that we've borrowed from phones.
And it's this little thing that sits on the cable that allows you to, uh, pause and play your music.
And if you double-click it twice, it goes to the next song.
And if you triple-click it, it goes back to the previous song.
And we've added volume controls.
Volume up and volume down.
So you can set the volume, you can go next and previous, and you can go play and pause all right from the headphone cable.
And on the back side, we have a microphone, which works beautifully with that voice recording app inside the Nano we saw a few minutes ago.
And so right from your headphone cable, you can control your whole Nano.
It's really nice.
And these headphones will ship for $29 next month.
We've also got some new in-ear headphones.
And, uh, these we think we finally got these right.
Uh, they ship with, uh, three sets of earbuds, uh, so you can pick exactly the ones that fit your ears, and they're, they've got two drivers each in them, a woofer and a tweeter at each side, which is something you normally don't find until you get pretty expensive headphones.
And these headphones are going to sell for $79 and they're going to be available in October.

So, the incredible new iPod Nanos.
Now, we've made a new ad, and if you'd like to see it, I'd be glad to run it.
Yeah?
All right, let's run it.

I tried to do handstands for you.
I tried to do handstands for you.
Every time I fell on you.
Yeah, every time I fell for you.
For you.

You like it?

I think that's going to be a lot of fun.
So, the new iPod Nanos, uh, catch them this week.
They're really, really nice.
So, let's move on to the iPod Touch.
The iPod Touch is an incredible product.
We've brought our, our multi-touch technology and our, our multi-touch user interface to an iPod.
And, uh, this is unlike, like anything in the marketplace.
Well, for this holiday season, we're making it even better.
And so this is the new iPod Touch.
It's got the same gorgeous 3 1/2 inch display, but it's even thinner.
It is this beautiful contoured stainless steel design.
And if you didn't think the last one could get thinner, you've got to get your hands on one of these things.
They're just fantastic.
And, uh, that's the bottom right there, the 30-pin connector.
And so, what's different about this?
Well, some things are the same, the stunning 3 1/2 inch display.
Here's something that's different.
This was the number one request we've gotten.
We've integrated volume controls into the side.
We think that's going to make a lot of people, uh, a little happier.
Of course, the accelerometer, wireless networking, 802.11b and g are still there.
We've built in a speaker, which is really hard with something this thin.
It's for casual listening.
Okay?
This is not for audio files, but it's really nice to have it.
Genius playlist creation right on the iPod Touch, and of course, the App Store built in.
So, let's take a look at some of these things.
We've enhanced the user interface a little bit.
Uh, it's a little nicer to scroll through lists of songs, better artwork on albums, and videos.
Of course, it's still great to watch video on the iPod Touch.
A little better for audio books.
So, the user interface is even nicer than it has been.
We've also built in Nike Plus iPod into the iPod Touch.
So, the software is all built in.
It's very nice.
And as you know, you need to plug in a receiver into the iPods to date to make it work with the transmitter puck that you put in your shoe.
Uh, not with the iPod Touch.
The receiver is actually built into the product itself.
So, all you have to do is get the, uh, the transmitter for your shoe and you're all set to go with Nike Plus iPod on the iPod Touch.

For, for genius, again, to be able to make these playlists from songs in the library right on the Touch that go great together.
We've built that right into the iPod Touch.
And so let's take a look.
If I'm listening to Don't Think Twice, It's All Right, I just tap to get the scrubber and, you know, the, the panel that lets me set, repeat and shuffle, and right, we've added right on there as you can see, a genius symbol.
You just tap that with your finger and you've made a genius playlist.
You can refresh it, you can save it.
As, if you save it, this is what it looks like.
It just lists the title of the seed song with the genius logo next to it, and you've got your genius playlist for as long as you want it.
So, genius playlist creation right on the iPod Touch.
And of course, the App Store.
This has been one of the most incredible phenomenons we've ever seen at Apple.
I am pleased to announce today that users have downloaded over 100 million apps from the App Store.

Now, this is mind-blowing.
But it's even more mind-blowing when you realize that today is only the 60th day it's been open.
The App Store opened 60 days ago today and 100 million apps have been downloaded.
That's pretty amazing and it's right on the iPod Touch.
All these incredible apps and most importantly, games.
Right?
There are about 700 games on the App Store today.
A lot of them for free.
And some of them are getting pretty fantastic.
I'm sure you've played some of these and know them well.
There's definitely something here for everybody.
And you can load them all up if you want on your iPod Touch.
And the App Store is available in 62 countries now.
And so that's pretty amazing on every iPod Touch.
So, let me show you some of this stuff.

So, I've got my iPod Touch here.
Let's turn it on.
And, uh, I'm going to go into music and I'm going to, uh, I'm going to pick Green Day.
Why not?
And, uh, American Idiot.
And I just tap it to bring up the on-screen controls and I'm going to hit the genius button.
You see it right there?
And I've just made a genius playlist here.
Right?
It's very cool.
And I can go ahead and I can refresh my playlist if I want, and get another list of 25 songs.
You know.
It's pretty nice.
Oops, excuse me.
There we go.
And, uh, so I can just make genius playlists right on my iPod Touch.
So, let me go to movies now and just, uh, remind you how great it is to see movies on an iPod Touch.
I've got Iron Man here.
And again, I can watch it in its full aspect ratio or double tap to fill the screen.
You get the idea.
And I can go to the App Store and download games and play all sorts of incredible games on my iPod Touch.
Uh, we've got a treat today.
Uh, I'm going to invite Phil Schiller up on stage.
Phil's our senior vice president of product marketing.

And Phil's, uh, Phil's going to give us a demo of some games that are not yet out on the market, one that just got out on the market.

And so go ahead and show us what you got.

All right.
So the new iPod Touch with the App Store built right in, all these other great features.
It works with the new headphones we have coming out next month as well.
And the battery life is just astounding.
36 hours of music and 6 hours of video all on this really thin iPod Touch.
And environmentally, the checklist looks a lot like the Nano.
Arsenic-free glass, BFR-free, mercury-free, PVC-free, and again, with the stainless steel and the glass, highly recyclable enclosure.
So we're really pleased with that.
So the new iPod Touch, it's got millions of songs that you can buy for it, thousands of Hollywood movies, and now hundreds of games.
This is the funnest iPod ever.
And we think people are going to really love it.

We've got it in three models.
We've got an 8 gigabyte model for a new much lower price of $229.

We've got a 16 gig model for $299.
That's double the memory for the same price as the old 8 gig used to be.
And a 32 gigabyte for $399.
And all three of these models are available starting today.
Now, we've got an ad for the iPod Touch too that I'd love to show you.
So let's run the ad.

The iPod Touch is the best portable device for listening to music.
It's clearly the best portable device for watching video.
And now, you can make a pretty good argument it's the best portable device for playing games on and a whole new class of games.
So we're very excited about it.
And this is the new iPod Touch for this holiday season.
Now, I'd like to talk for a minute about the software on these devices.
The new iPod Touch has a new version of software called 2.1.
And uh you could see some of the the new things that it could do.
Well, what if you have the first generation iPod Touch?
Well, you can get version 2.1 as well.
If you've upgraded to 2.0, it's a free update to 2.1.
If you haven't, it's $9.95 to update to 2.1 from a 1.x release.
And these updates are available today.
Just go to apple.com.
In addition to that, if you have an iPhone, we have a new release of software for the iPhone, 2.1 software update.
Now 2.1 software update's a big update.
It fixes lots of bugs.
Uh you'll get fewer call drops.
Uh you will get a significantly improved battery life for most customers.
Uh we have fixed a lot of bugs where if you have a lot of apps on the phone, you're not going to get some of the crashes and other things that we've seen.
Backing up to iTunes is dramatically faster.
And so just a lot of bugs have been fixed.

And there's some some great new performance enhancements as well.
So 2.1 software update's a big one for the iPhone.
It is free uh to all iPhone owners and it is going to be available this Friday.
So, keep an eye out for it later this week.
It's a really good update if you have an iPhone.
So, that's software.
So back to iPod plus iTunes.
We think we've got the best lineup we've ever had for this holiday season.
We enter this holiday season at the end of June having sold over 160 million iPods and having the strongest lineup of iPods we've ever had for holiday season before.
And having the best version of iTunes we've ever had.
So we're ready for this holiday season with iPod plus iTunes.
And we really appreciate the chance to share this with you this morning.
Thank you.

Now, whenever we have a music event, uh we think it's really important to remind ourselves and and all of our our customers why we do this in the first place.
And the reason we do this all is because like you, we love music.
And it just gets us really excited when we can we can uh bring some products to market that make enjoying music even better.
Well, today we've got a really special guest uh who's uh agreed to come and perform for us.
He's sold over 16 million albums.
His tour was one of the hottest tickets this summer.
And he's the number one selling male artist in iTunes history.
So can you please join me in giving a great welcome to Jack Johnson.
